title: ramshared-coco-result/v1
description: One CoCo platform row attempt against the pinned VMBus ring-buffer upstream v2 candidate. A result is an evidence record, not a verdict about the series. Statuses are never rewritten: PARTIAL, NO_RESULT and ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE are terminal facts and are never upgraded to PASS by a later document edit. Infrastructure status and qualification status are separate fields on purpose; a lost guest is not a hardware gate result.

schema.description: Schema identity. Bump only on a breaking change to the evidence contract.

run_id.description: Stable identifier of the qualification session, distinct from any CI job id. Re-running the same row creates a new run_id.

attempt.description: 1-based attempt number for this row within this run_id. Every attempt is preserved; a failed attempt is never overwritten by a later successful one.

job.description: CI job or lab-session identifier if the run was orchestrated remotely. Omitted for a hand-run bundle.

executor.description: Who ran it: a lab name, a volunteer handle, or 'operator'. Never a personal email address in a shared artifact.

bundle_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the shipped tester bundle tarball, so a result is attributable to the exact instructions it followed.

candidate.description: Byte identity of what was booted. A result whose candidate fields do not match the current CANDIDATE-MANIFEST is evidence about different bytes and cannot be cited about the current series.

series_base.description: Mainline base commit the series applies on.

series_tip.description: Scratch-tree tip that produced the patch bytes.

patch_sha256s.description: SHA-256 of 0001 through 0014 in order. Exactly fourteen, never the cover.

series_sha256sums_ok.description: True only if sha256sum -c was run inside series/ in the guest and every line reported OK. A locally computed hash is not this field.

config_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the kernel .config used to build the booted image.

diagnostic_delta.description: Any patch or config change that is NOT part of the fourteen production bytes, used only to gather diagnostics. Must be marked experimental and must never be folded into a production claim. null when the candidate was unmodified.

row.description: Which matrix row this attempt addresses. COCO-4 and COCO-5 are exercised on the same platform as the base row and are reported as their own attempts, not folded into a COCO-1 PASS.

capability.description: What the guest actually reported about its isolation. A CPU flag alone is never a capability proof: a paravisor can filter it. An unknown mode is unqualified and maps the attempt to ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE, never to a platform PASS.

claimed_platform.description: What the tester believed they provisioned. Evidence, not authority: isolation_mode is the authority.

isolation_mode.description: What the guest proved. 'unknown' is a valid terminal value. 'tdx_paravisor' is a different row from COCO-2 and cannot close it.

isolation_proof.description: Verbatim guest log lines that establish the isolation mode, e.g. the dmesg activation line. Never a SKU name, never a runner label, never a flag list alone.

paravisor.description: Paravisor presence as reported by the guest. 'absent' is required for COCO-2. 'unknown' is not 'absent'.

paravisor_evidence.description: Verbatim lines supporting the paravisor field, including the negative. Empty only when paravisor is 'unknown'.

confidential_vmbus_offers.description: Which confidential VMBus offers the guest observed. 'unknown' is not 'none'. A private ring is never decrypted merely to force shared-path coverage.

preflight_report_path.description: Path to the coco-capability-preflight.sh key=value report, relative to the bundle root. Must exist as an attached artifact.

infrastructure_status.description: Did the run finish on its own? This is not a qualification verdict. 'completed' is required before any PASS is even schema-valid.

infrastructure_note.description: What happened operationally. A timeout or a lost guest is recorded here as a fact; it is never reported as a cause of a test failure unless a log line names that cause.

qualification_status.description: The row's evidence state. Never rewritten to PASS by a later document edit. NO_RESULT means the run did not produce a readable outcome; ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE means the platform was never available; PARTIAL means some named subcheck ran and others did not; FAIL means a named subcheck produced negative evidence.

status_justification.description: Why this status and not another. Required for every status, including PASS. Must name the counters and phases that support it. A causal claim requires a log line that names the cause; an inference is labelled as a hypothesis, never as the cause.

counters.description: Named observations with a phase. Never a synthesized score. Every number cited in any downstream document must appear here first; a number that is not in this array has not been measured.

subchecks.description: The named before→action→after checks for this row. A subcheck may be 'not_run'; it is never inferred from a sibling.

artifacts.description: Files attached to this result, each with a SHA-256. Paths are relative to the bundle root; no absolute host workspace path may appear.

log_safety.description: NFR-3 attestation. A result that carries a kernel virtual address is not acceptable evidence.

attested_by.description: Who ran the strip check. May be the executor.

notes.description: Free-form observations that are not counters. Do not put a verdict here that is not in qualification_status.

name.description: The exact counter name as the tool prints it. Never a paraphrase, never a category like 'leaks'.

phase.description: When it was observed. A before/after pair is two counters with the same name and different phases, not one delta.

value.description: The observed value. A string is allowed only for a non-numeric observation and must state what was seen.

unit.description: count, bytes, ms, percent, boolean, line, or a named unit. 'count' for integers with no physical dimension.

source.description: How it was observed: the command and the field, e.g. 'vmbus-lifecycle-drill.sh log: PHASE1-AFTER maps_count', or 'dmesg: count of BUG:'. Relative paths only.

required_for_pass.description: True when this counter must be present and satisfy a threshold for the row to be PASS. The threshold lives in the row's subcheck, not here.

result.description: 'inconclusive' is not 'pass'. 'not_run' is not 'fail'. A subcheck is never inherited from a different row or a different attempt.

evidence.description: Verbatim log lines or named artifact references supporting this result. Required even for 'not_run' (name what was attempted and why it was not run).

before.description: The 'before' observation of the before→action→after triple, or null when the subcheck has no before/after shape.

after.description: The 'after' observation, or null. Before and after must describe the same counter name.

path.description: Bundle-relative path. Leading slash and '..' are rejected: a result must not name a host workspace path.

allOf.$comment: PASS is only schema-valid when the platform was proven, the run completed on its own, and the guest never saw a BUG, Oops or panic. This is the structural form of the rule that a lost guest or an unproven platform can never be reported as a hardware gate PASS.
COCO-2 additionally requires a proven absence of a paravisor. A paravisor run is a different row and is never a COCO-2 PASS.
ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE means the platform was never available. It carries no counters that would imply a run happened.
A lost guest or a provisioner failure is an infrastructure fact. It can produce NO_RESULT or PARTIAL, never PASS, and never a bare FAIL that asserts a code defect.
